comment: Pinned source registry for the automated cadence. Every entry maps a primary source to the matrix rows whose status depends on it. Adding a source here is the only way to bring it under automated watch; see docs/agent-cadence.md.

sources.title: Microsoft Purview DLP for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat
sources.note: Backing docs repository MicrosoftDocs/Purview-pr is not public (raw fetch returned HTTP 404 on 2026-08-07), so HTML fingerprinting is required for this source. Re-probe periodically: if a public mirror appears, switch mode to 'markdown'.

sources.title: AI threat protection in Microsoft Defender for Cloud
sources.note: Backing docs repository MicrosoftDocs/defender-docs is public (raw fetch returned HTTP 200 on 2026-08-07). Watching the source markdown avoids rendered-page navigation churn entirely. cite_url is the Microsoft Learn URL that must appear in the matrix; the raw URL is a fetch mechanism only and is never cited as a primary source.

sources.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud release notes
sources.note: Carries the dated GA / Preview entries that evidence row 4's status dates. This page also carries dozens of release notes for products outside this repository's scope (containers, SQL, Kubernetes); without relevance_filter the fingerprint would change on almost every run and the detector would escalate constantly for entries that cannot affect any matrix row.

sources.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud release notes archive
sources.note: Holds the dated 'General Availability for Defender for AI Services - May 1, 2025' entry that row 4's GA date rests on. Added on 2026-08-07 after the citation-containment validator found this URL cited in the matrix but absent from the registry.

sources.title: Microsoft 365 Roadmap feature 548671
sources.note: The per-feature endpoint (/api/v1/m365/features/<id>) returned HTTP 404 on 2026-08-07; the collection endpoint returned HTTP 200 and contains the feature. The watcher fetches the collection and selects by feature_id.

sources.title: Considerations for deploying Microsoft Purview Data Security Posture Management
sources.note: The current (non-classic) DSPM considerations page. Carries the prerequisite list and the only licensing sentence Microsoft offers for the current version, which names no SKU and defers to the Purview service description. Backing docs repository MicrosoftDocs/Purview-pr is not public (raw fetch returned HTTP 404 on 2026-08-10), so HTML fingerprinting is required.

sources.title: Microsoft Purview service description
sources.note: The other end of row 6's circular licensing reference: the DSPM page points here for licensing, and this page points back at the DSPM article. Watched so that either side gaining an actual SKU statement is detected. relevance_filter keeps the fingerprint from churning on the rest of this large, multi-solution service description.

sources.title: Learn about Data Security Posture Management for AI (classic)
sources.note: Documents the default-posture behaviour row 7 records (audit mode only; blocking policy shipped in test mode). Learn marks this article the classic version, replaced by a new one. Watched precisely because a classic page is where a silent behavioural divergence would appear.

sources.title: Considerations for deploying DSPM for AI (classic)
sources.note: Carries every load-bearing quote behind row 7's audit-mode-only finding, plus the third-party-AI-site dependency text. Added on 2026-08-10 after an independent verification pass found those quotes were verbatim but cited to pages that do not contain them -- the same class of gap sources.json:42 records for the release-notes archive. Also reachable via a 301 from /purview/ai-microsoft-purview-considerations.

sources.title: Microsoft Purview data security and compliance protections for AI
sources.note: Carries row 7's self-contradiction: this single page calls the new DSPM both 'the preview version' and 'the current version of DSPM'. Watched so that the contradiction being resolved is detected -- that resolution is what would let row 7 leave Requires further validation, after in-tenant confirmation by a human.

sources.title: Cloud app catalog and risk scores (Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps)
sources.note: The only Learn page carrying all of: the catalog size figure, the Generative AI category definition, and the adjacent AI - MCP Server and AI - Model Provider categories. There is no Learn article dedicated to generative-AI app discovery, so this page is the whole primary source for row 8's capability claim.

sources.title: Discovered apps (Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps)
sources.note: Source of row 8's platform-coverage sentence ('Supported apps include Windows and macOS apps'). Watched alongside the catalog page because the macOS claim is contradicted by the Defender for Endpoint integration article, and a change on either side settles that.

sources.title: Find your Microsoft Sentinel data connector
relevance_filter: data connectors are currently in Preview
sources.note: No dedicated Learn page exists for a Sentinel Microsoft Copilot connector -- six candidate URLs returned HTTP 404 on 2026-08-10 and the solutions catalog contains no occurrence of 'Copilot' -- so row 9 rests on this aggregate reference page's collapsible entry. relevance_filter is essential: the page is ~1.7 MB and lists hundreds of connectors, so an unfiltered fingerprint would change on nearly every run for entries that cannot affect any matrix row. The filter deliberately also matches the page-level 'currently in Preview' notice, which is one half of row 9's conflict.

sources.title: MITRE ATLAS distributed dataset (ATLAS.yaml)
sources.note: Watches the dataset version the cross-walk's technique IDs are verified against, so a dataset bump is detected rather than noticed by hand. Three things worth knowing. (1) watch_only keeps this out of allowed_citation_urls: it backs no capability row and must not enlarge what an automated run may cite. (2) crosswalk_rows is documentation for humans -- no script reads it -- because a framework source backs a cross-walk row, not a matrix row, and matrix_rows is optional in the code. (3) This is the first fetch origin in this registry outside microsoft.com and MicrosoftDocs. A watcher target cannot be pinned to a commit the way an action can, so the compensating control is the shape guard on what a version_pattern may capture, in scripts/watch_sources.py.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications -- current edition landing page
crosswalk_rows: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications framework-versions row
sources.note: Fingerprints the set of item IDs the landing page presents, because an edition change replaces every one of them at once -- a far tighter signal than a page hash. KNOWN LIMITATION, stated rather than implied: this page lags. On 2026-08-09 it still presented the 2025 edition while the 2026 edition was already published (crosswalk/framework-crosswalk.md records this), so detection here is late, not immediate. The alternative is worse: each edition has its own resource URL, so watching the current edition's page would never fire for the next one. Treat a change here as confirmation, never as the earliest possible warning.

human_only_sources.title: Microsoft 365 Message Center
human_only_sources.reason: Message Center posts are tenant-scoped and have no public URL (docs/how-to-read-status.md). Reading them would require a tenant credential in repository secrets and would introduce tenant-scoped data, which disclaimer.md and the README confidentiality note forbid. This source is therefore permanently human-only and is never fetched by any workflow.

human_only_sources.title: CSA AI Controls Matrix (AICM) spreadsheet
human_only_sources.reason: Published only inside a registration-gated spreadsheet on the CSA artifact page (crosswalk/framework-crosswalk.md). Not machine-fetchable; control-ID mappings must be re-verified by a human against the AICM workbook.

human_only_sources.title: NIST AI 600-1 -- Generative AI Profile
human_only_sources.reason: A static, dated PDF with no edition churn a fingerprint could see. Watching it would report 'unchanged' forever and be mistaken for coverage: a successor document appears at a NEW URL, which no fingerprint of the old one can detect. Recorded here so the gap is documented rather than invisible -- noticing a successor is a human step at the monthly refresh.
